topic: Contesting, DX, remote operation and mesh networks

questions.question: What indicator is required to be used by US-licensed operators when operating a station via remote control and the remote transmitter is located in the US?

choices.A: / followed by the USPS two-letter abbreviation for the state in which the remote station is located
choices.B: /R# where # is the district of the remote station
choices.C: / followed by the ARRL Section of the remote station

questions.question: Which of the following file formats is used for exchanging amateur radio log data?
From which of the following bands is amateur radio contesting generally excluded?
Which of the following frequencies can be used for amateur radio mesh networks?

choices.A: HF frequencies where digital communications are permitted
choices.B: Frequencies shared with various unlicensed wireless data services
choices.D: The 60-meter band channel centered on 5373 kHz

questions.answer: Frequencies shared with various unlicensed wireless data services

questions.question: What is the function of a DX QSL Manager?

choices.B: Handle the receiving and sending of confirmations for a DX station
choices.C: Run a net to allow many stations to contact a rare DX station
choices.D: Communicate to a DXpedition about propagation, band openings, pileup conditions, etc.

questions.answer: Handle the receiving and sending of confirmations for a DX station

questions.question: During a VHF/UHF contest, in which band segment would you expect to find the highest level of SSB or CW activity?

choices.A: At the top of each band, usually in a segment reserved for contests
choices.B: In the middle of each band, usually on the national calling frequency
choices.C: In the weak signal segment of the band, with most of the activity near the calling frequency
choices.D: In the middle of the band, usually 25 kHz above the national calling frequency

questions.answer: In the weak signal segment of the band, with most of the activity near the calling frequency

questions.question: What is the Cabrillo format?

choices.A: A standard for submission of electronic contest logs
choices.B: A method of exchanging information during a contest QSO
choices.C: The most common set of contest rules
choices.D: A digital protocol specifically designed for rapid contest exchanges

questions.answer: A standard for submission of electronic contest logs

questions.question: Which of the following contacts may be confirmed through the Logbook of The World (LoTW)?

choices.A: Special event contacts between stations in the US
choices.B: Contacts between a US station and a non-US station
choices.C: Contacts for Worked All States credit

questions.question: What type of equipment is commonly used to implement an amateur radio mesh network?

choices.A: A 2-meter VHF transceiver with a 1,200-baud modem
choices.B: A computer running EchoLink to provide interface from the radio to the internet
choices.C: A wireless router running custom firmware
choices.D: A 440 MHz transceiver with a 9,600-baud modem

questions.answer: A wireless router running custom firmware

questions.question: Why do DX stations often transmit and receive on different frequencies?

choices.A: Because the DX station may be transmitting on a frequency that is prohibited to some responding stations
choices.B: To separate the calling stations from the DX station
choices.C: To improve operating efficiency by reducing interference

questions.question: How should you generally identify your station when attempting to contact a DX station during a contest or in a pileup?

choices.A: Send your full call sign once or twice
choices.B: Send only the last two letters of your call sign until you make contact
choices.C: Send your full call sign and grid square
choices.D: Send the call sign of the DX station three times, the words “this is,” then your call sign three times

questions.answer: Send your full call sign once or twice
